title: Hindi
description: Everyday Hindi in Devanagari with romanization: greetings, family, food, numbers, travel and your day.

units.title: Greetings
units.description: Say hello, introduce yourself and be polite.
units.tip: 'नमस्ते' (namaste) works for hello and goodbye. 'आप' (aap) is the polite 'you'; 'तुम' (tum) is for friends.

units.title: People and family
units.description: Talk about the people around you.
units.tip: Words like 'my' change with the noun's gender: 'मेरा बेटा' (mera beta, my son) but 'मेरी बेटी' (meri beti, my daughter).

units.title: Food and drink
units.tip: Many verbs change with the speaker's gender: a man says 'पीता हूँ' (peeta hoon), a woman 'पीती हूँ' (peeti hoon).

units.title: Numbers
units.description: Count from one to ten, ask prices and tell the time.
units.tip: To tell the time use 'बजे' (baje): 'तीन बजे हैं' (teen baje hain) = it is three o'clock.

units.title: Travel and directions
units.description: Find your way around a new city.
units.tip: Hindi puts the verb at the end: 'होटल कहाँ है?' (hotal kahaan hai) = hotel where is?

units.title: Daily routine
units.description: Home, work, school and the time of day.
units.tip: 'कल' (kal) means both tomorrow and yesterday - the verb tense tells you which one.
